title: Max und Moritz
author: Wilhelm Busch
blurb: Seven rhyming pranks by two naughty boys, and what finally happens to them.
note: Published in 1865 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Wilhelm Busch, Max and Moritz, from Max und Moritz, 1865. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Der Struwwelpeter
author: Heinrich Hoffmann
blurb: Short rhymed warnings for children: the boy who plays with matches, the one who will not eat his soup.
note: Published in 1845 and the author died in 1894, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Heinrich Hoffmann, Struwwelpeter, the title figure of Der Struwwelpeter, 1845. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Grimms Märchen (Auswahl)
author: Jacob und Wilhelm Grimm
blurb: Nine of the best-known fairy tales, from the Frog King and Hansel and Gretel to Snow White and Rumpelstiltskin.
note: Collected and published from 1812 to 1857 by authors who died in 1859 and 1863, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The text is that of a 1921 edition, in the spelling of its day.
coverCredit: Arthur Rackham, Hansel and Gretel at the witch’s house, for the Grimms’ fairy tales, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Heidi (Auswahl)
author: Johanna Spyri
blurb: Five-year-old Heidi is brought up the mountain to live with her gruff grandfather and spends her first summer with the goats. The first three chapters.
note: Published in 1880 and the author died in 1901, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is modernized.
coverCredit: Giovanni Segantini, Midday in the Alps, 1891. Segantini Museum, St. Moritz. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Fabeln (Auswahl)
author: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
blurb: Forty-six short prose fables about foxes, ravens, wolves and donkeys, each with a sharp point. Most are only a few lines long.
note: Published in 1759 and the author died in 1781, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Franz Marc, The Foxes, 1913. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Immensee
author: Theodor Storm
blurb: An old man remembers the girl he loved as a boy and the lake where they last met.
note: Published in 1849 and the author died in 1888, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Caspar David Friedrich, Woman before the Setting Sun, about 1818. Museum Folkwang, Essen. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Die Verwandlung
author: Franz Kafka
blurb: Gregor Samsa wakes up one morning as a giant insect and his family has to cope.
note: Published in 1915 and the author died in 1924, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Albrecht Dürer, Stag Beetle, 1505. J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Siddhartha
author: Hermann Hesse
blurb: A young Brahmin leaves home in India to look for peace and finds it in an unexpected place.
note: Published in 1922, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Liang Kai, Shakyamuni Emerging from the Mountains, 13th century. Tokyo National Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Kleider machen Leute
author: Gottfried Keller
blurb: A poor tailor in a fine cloak is taken for a Polish count in a small Swiss town and never finds the right moment to tell the truth.
note: Published in 1874 and the author died in 1890, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Carl Spitzweg, The Arrival of the Stagecoach, about 1859. Grohmann Museum, Milwaukee. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Die Leiden des jungen Werther
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: The letters of a sensitive young man who falls in love with a woman who is already engaged.
note: Published in 1774 and revised in 1787, by an author who died in 1832, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Wilhelm Amberg, Reading Goethe’s Werther, 1870. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Effi Briest
author: Theodor Fontane
blurb: A young woman marries an older Prussian official and pays for one mistake for the rest of her life.
note: Published in 1895 and the author died in 1898, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Caspar David Friedrich, Woman at a Window, 1822. Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Faust. Der Tragödie erster Teil
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
blurb: The scholar Faust makes a wager with the devil Mephistopheles and wins the love of young Gretchen, with tragic results. A play in verse.
note: Published in 1808 by an author who died in 1832, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Georg Friedrich Kersting, Faust in His Study, 1829. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Der Tod in Venedig
author: Thomas Mann
blurb: An aging, famous writer travels to Venice, falls under the spell of a beautiful boy, and stays on as cholera spreads through the city.
note: Published in 1912, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). The author died in 1955, so it is also in the public domain where copyright lasts 70 years after death.
coverCredit: Claude Monet, San Giorgio Maggiore, Twilight, 1908. National Museum Cardiff. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
